This is probably my favorite game of all time, and I have at least double the hours in this then any other (Steam is showing about 1200 right now if that's important to you).

I adore the Don't Starve series, and DST (Don't Starve Together) especially. It's a fantastic game with significantly more content then it looks like.  I've been playing on an off since 2016 and there's always something new to work on or seek out (seriously there's a major update at least a few times a year with free content).  The game lore is incredible, and well worth the time to understand and play toward.  Not exactly a "horror" or "spooky" game, but it has a very cool Tim-Burton-esq art style and I have also found it fun to listen to halloween music while playing to heighten the ~vibes~.

Most aspects of the game are customizable in game and world gen settings. So you can turn off frog rain if it's the bane of your Spring seasons, or play in an eternal autumn as one of my friends has done.  You can increases bosses to lots, or turn out the lights for an entirely different run. If you just want to hang out and farm (with the incredibly complex farming system) you totally can, or you can completely ignore the mechanic all together.  Whatever you like best you can spend time on, and if making a base or hunting bosses, or seafaring isn't up your alley there's enough content to skip your least favorite parts and still have so so much to do.  But you'll have a more complete experience if you try a bit of everything. I have found that generally DST rewards time and knowledge spent, and the more difficult an enemy or obstacle appears, the more rewarding it is to conquer (and the better the loot too)!

That said, this is a survival game, and it is hard. When players say everything can kill you, we're not exaggerating.  There's a steep learning curve, especially from brand new to intermediate, and the game itself gives you little to no instruction. Don't panic. Part of the fun is experimenting and (probably) dying to something silly.  (But if you want more explanation there are many amazing guides out there; I'm partial to the youtube ones myself.) If you're not a hardcore gamer, or don't pick up on gaming things quickly, same!  I've been able to have so much fun at a beginner level and I still think this is worth it.  If you're a more advanced player there are some really cool raid bosses to take on that I think you'll really enjoy. If you're into mods, there are many and they are super easily applied to the game (via Steam Workshop).  Honestly, this game was the first I played with mods, and I'm sad every time I add mods to anything else because it's so much more work lol.  I typically play solo, but multiplayer is active and enjoyable when I can convince people to play with me lol.  I have found that it's generally good to get the basics down solo before attempting to play with others but ymmv.

If DST is looking too overwhelming, maybe check out Don't Starve first.  I really think this series is worth the effort, time, and money and if Together seems too far out of your skill level, the single player games might a better fit for you.  Enemies have significantly lower heath pools, and the vanilla Don't Starve has a lot less going on in general.  A great place to start if the art and story are interesting but you're not as interested in combat.

I almost always play on my desktop but I have also played on a laptop as well as a Nintendo Switch (but not a Steam Deck, so might be different) and I found handheld/console really frustrating.  It might be because I've put so many hours on pc that console controls really messed up my playing, but gameplay became clunky and overall less suited to controller or handheld gaming then I would have preferred.  I really wouldn't suggest this as a game to play on an already slow laptop, but any desktop and most laptops of middling speed/quality should be able to handle it.  If you have a slow laptop (like mine was rip) the game will likely play, but the lag could be anywhere from workable to almost inoperable.  Btw, this is exponentially compounded if you are trying to play with others.  For example: a slow-ish game solo might become unplayable with a friend on the server even if by yourself it's doable.

Look at these subjects! They build stone walls, hoard food in chests, and pray to a science machine as if it might grant them salvation. They believe that if they only toil hard enough, Winter will spare them.
But the Shadow is already here. It sits right behind them, waiting for that pathetic sanity meter to drop. The game offers no promise of victory - only a brief reprieve.
True wisdom lies not in constructing an impregnable fortress, but in building a campfire, sitting beside it, listening to the logs crackle, and accepting that, come morning, you must venture back into the cold, unforgiving woods. Not for the sake of some grand purpose, but simply because this is the rhythm of the world - a rhythm that possesses a strange, harsh beauty. It is a mechanism that establishes an obsessive-compulsive structure through a cycle of resource management, where the "Other" manifests as an impersonal Law of lack, and *jouissance* is tethered to the ritual of averting catastrophe. It is the position of an obsessive captive to ritual: you act - not to gain recognition or reach a conclusion, but because to stop would mean confronting the Real - the very thing the ritual was designed to forestall. In this sense, *Don't Starve Together* constructs an obsessive position: a subject caught between anxiety and fleeting relief. Here, the subject attempts to govern the Real through ritual - a process structurally akin to a neurotic’s endeavor to cope with lack.

Bermain Don't Starve Together (DST) bersama teman adalah salah satu pengalaman co-op survival terbaik yang pernah saya rasakan. Gim ini tidak sekadar menuntut kita untuk mencari makan, tetapi juga bertahan dari kejamnya perubahan musim dan berbagai ancaman monster yang tidak terduga.

Kedalaman mekanik gim ini sangat memuaskan. Manajemen inventaris, rotasi cuaca—mulai dari musim dingin yang membekukan hingga musim panas yang rawan kebakaran—serta variasi bos membuat setiap sesi bermain selalu menantang. Mati berkali-kali di gim ini adalah hal biasa, dan itu justru menjadi pelajaran berharga untuk mengatur strategi base-building yang lebih matang di ronde berikutnya.

Namun, hal yang paling patut diapresiasi dari DST adalah dedikasi luar biasa dari pihak developer, Klei Entertainment. Untuk sebuah gim yang dirilis bertahun-tahun lalu, mereka masih sangat konsisten memberikan update konten masif, rework karakter, serta event musiman secara gratis sampai detik ini. Perhatian dan komitmen mereka terhadap komunitas pemain benar-benar mantap.

Secara keseluruhan, dengan harga yang sangat terjangkau (terlebih sering ada diskon yang otomatis memberikan ekstra satu copy untuk diberikan ke teman), DST adalah sebuah masterpiece. Jika Kalian mencari tantangan survival yang sesungguhnya dan punya teman untuk diajak menjadi idiot bersama, gim ini wajib ada di library kalian. 10/10.

我不喜欢现在的《饥荒》，尤其是看到最近暗影线最终BOSS的更新之后，这种感觉更明显了。《饥荒》既然宣发时定位是“科技与魔法的生存游戏”，那我觉得最有乐趣的部分，就是不断解锁科技进度、往家里摆东西、慢慢把营地建设起来。可游戏一到中后期就开始变味：一开始游戏定位要素被不断剥离，逐渐变成一款RPG战斗游戏。论同样的操作维度，暗黑破坏神不比这种缺乏交互感的BOSS战好玩得多？我期待的流水线呢？生存游戏后期该有的产能循环呢？我甚至觉得，做成塔防、防御鱼人和狗等敌对兽潮，再把猪人作为NPC做任务线，都更符合一开始的宣发方向。我要的是科技、魔法和生存，是摆东西和建设的乐趣；现在这些乐趣被剥离了，就像蛋糕店里卖的蛋糕突然变成了面包——我凭什么要尝，还要勉强说好吃？

还有数值平衡也一言难尽，某位“TOO STRONG”我都懒得喷。更新方向不清不楚就算了，但凡能听进一半意见，也不至于有这么多人喷。
